Iris: heads-up - I'm prepping a docs PR to add a decision matrix: when to use prefetch vs large-batching vs small-batching for Optimize toolkit. Will include JS + Rust snippets, migration note for renamed qprofiles, and a tiny ops checklist for canarying. Need reviewers: @Jorge (SDK), @Nina (perf), and someone from QA to run eval harness.

Jorge: nice. Favor adding a short example showing streaming with prefetch turned on vs off (latency comparison). I can review JS snippet.

Iris: good call. draft JS snippet (to land in examples):
```js
// JS prefetch example
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD })
const resp = await client.optimize.prefetch({
  model: 'rwd-open-7b-quant',
  prefetchKeys: ['session_history'],
  batchSize: 6,
  quantProfile: 'qprofile-lowlat-v1',
})
console.log(resp.summary())
```

Nina: I'll run the eval harness. please add the CLI command I should run and the expected rough outputs for 8/32/512 tokens so I can sanity check.

Iris: CLI I used locally: `tools/eval/harness --suite=kv-prefetch-matrix --model=rwd-open-7b-quant --tokens=8,32,512 --runs=30 --out=results.json` Expected KPIs: median latency per token, p95 latency, and tokens/sec. I'll include a tiny sample table in the PR (approx numbers).

Leo: for Rust snippet I can help tidy. Quick heads-up: our Rust SDK changed the Optimize() method last week. Use `optimize_client()` instead of `Optimize()` or add a compatibility note.

Iris: drafting Rust example now:
```rust
// Rust prefetch example
use redwood::Client;
let client = Client::new(std::env::var("REDWOOD").unwrap());
let opts = redwood::opt::PrefetchOptions::builder()
    .model("rwd-open-7b-quant")
    .prefetch_keys(vec!["session_history".into()])
    .batch_size(6)
    .quant_profile("qprofile-lowlat-v1")
    .build();
let res = client.optimize_client().prefetch(opts).await?;
println!("{:?}", res.summary());
```

Jorge: minor nit: mention the newer qprofile names and map old->new in a small table. Also add runtime fallback snippet: if qprofile missing, route traffic to `rwd-open-7b` non-quant model.

Iris: adding mapping and fallback code sample. Also adding a one-paragraph decision rule for infra: prefer prefetch when user context is stable across requests; prefer large-batching for bursty throughput-oriented workloads.

Nina: results (quick summary): 8 tokens -> median latency 12ms/token, p95 28ms, 32 tokens -> median 10ms/token, p95 35ms (prefetch shows ~15% lower latency vs no-prefetch in short sequences), 512 tokens -> batching gives better throughput, prefetch adds modest memory overhead. Uploading full CSV.
